report.clinical_summary: Patient with CLL diagnosed about a year ago, currently in early stages with minimal symptoms. Not on any medication for CLL, following a watch-and-wait approach with regular hematologist follow-up every three months. Reports increased fatigue affecting work and evening family time, and a new lump under the chin. Has made lifestyle adjustments including being more cautious about physical activity and incorporating stress-management techniques. Trusts their hematologist and believes in the effectiveness of medical treatment.

evidence.quote: I've been having trouble staying up late to spend time with my kids after work — I usually feel exhausted around 9 pm
It's definitely affecting my quality of life and family time
I've definitely noticed that the fatigue can make it harder for me to get through a full day of work
There have been days where I've had to take a nap in the afternoon just to recharge, and that's not something I used to do before my diagnosis
I'm also more cautious about being physically active — I'll try to go for walks or gentle exercise but won't push myself too hard like I used to with sports

consequences.reasoning: The patient has made significant lifestyle adjustments due to fatigue - taking afternoon naps, being more cautious about physical activity, and having trouble with evening activities with family. This shows moderate impact on their daily life and roles.

evidence.quote: I was diagnosed about a year ago
Since then, I've just been following up with my hematologist every three months or so
The hematologist said that since my condition is still in the early stages, we can wait-and-see how things go for now
I know that living with CLL will be an ongoing process
I try not to dwell too much on what could happen. But at the same time, I do think about it and make plans accordingly

timeline.reasoning: The patient understands CLL as an ongoing process and is following a watch-and-wait approach. They acknowledge it will continue but don't dwell on specific timelines.

evidence.quote: I try not to let it consume me, though, and instead focus on taking care of myself as best I can in the meantime

It's all about finding that balance between being active and not overdoing it
For now, I'm just focusing on staying as healthy as possible and enjoying life as best I can given the circumstances

personal_control.reasoning: The patient actively manages their health through self-care practices, diet, rest, and stress management. They're making conscious choices about activity levels and planning for the future.
